items.name: Ming city wall bike ride
items.detail: Sandra's Xi'an standout, and the right thing to do on a jet-lagged first afternoon because it asks nothing of you but pedalling. Y45 for three hours then Y5 per extra ten minutes; deposit Y200. Six rental stations, 13.7 km around, two to three hours. Return to any station until 20:00; after that everything goes back to South Gate (永宁门), open until 22:00, evening returns by 21:30. Check both brakes before you ride off — hers had one.

items.name: Muslim Quarter after dark
items.detail: The other easy win, a short walk from the wall's north side.

items.name: Terracotta Warriors
items.detail: Three pits, still being excavated, nothing air-conditioned — which matters far less in October than it did in Sandra's July. Y120, 08:30–17:00, so it's a morning start. Pit 2 has been half-closed for works since 5 September under a notice running about a month.

items.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda fountain show
items.detail: North square, five minutes' walk from the Westin. Good for an evening with nothing left in you.

items.name: Small Wild Goose Pagoda & Xi'an Museum
items.detail: The fallback if the Shaanxi History Museum release fails: free, quiet and never sell out.

items.name: The tea ceremony scam
items.detail: Sandra fell for this one. The tell is someone asking you to take a photo OF THEM — locals who approach Westerners want to be in the picture. If a friendly stranger steers the conversation toward tea, walk away mid-sentence.

items.name: Urban Planning Exhibition Center
items.detail: Top of Sandra's ranking. Closed for a long renovation after her visit and reopened in 2022 — now free but on a timed booking through its WeChat mini-programme, 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:00, shut WEDNESDAYS. Booking opens seven days out, so Sunday the 11th means 4 October, while you're between Shigatse and base camp.

items.name: Propaganda Poster Art Centre
items.detail: No longer the apartment-block basement Sandra found — moved in 2019 to the seventh floor of 726 Yan'an West Road. Y25, 10:00–17:00, still barely signposted, opens daily. Nine-minute walk from Jiangsu Road, which is on your own Line 11.

items.name: The Bund, then Yu Gardens
items.detail: The Bund for the Art Deco and the live jazz; Yu Gardens and the bird-and-cricket market if there's daylight left. Skip the Railway Museum.

items.name: The Suzhou question
items.detail: Thirty minutes from Shanghai Railway Station or Hongqiao, trains every few minutes, passport is enough to board. Sandra rated the Suzhou Silk Museum among the best museums she saw anywhere in China, and the station puts you near the Humble Administrator's Garden and the Suzhou Museum. The obvious day trip — but it doesn't fit either plan without displacing a park day, and from a Disney-side hotel it's a 90-minute journey before you've started. Only if you drop to two park days.

items.name: Quanjude for roast duck
items.detail: Ask for Todd Wong, +86 135 2433 8834, introduced via Sandra's old boss Bob Isaacson. Much better with a group, so it suits Shanghai more than solo Xi'an.

items.name: Sandra's blog is private
items.detail: walltowall2017.wordpress.com — 70 entries, 10 May to 25 July 2017, locked to approved followers since her 26 June 2017 post. WebFetch, curl and the WordPress public API all fail; it only opens from a browser already signed into an approved WordPress.com account. All 70 were read on 9 September and the relevant material distilled into the Sandra-2017 page.

items.name: Her warnings held; her logistics didn't
items.detail: On 10 September every operational detail taken from the 2017 blog was re-checked against current sources. What changed: the Terracotta metro route, hours, booking channel and the loss of its ticket windows; the Shaanxi History Museum's reservation system, website route and suspended Monday closure; the city wall's rental terms; the Propaganda Poster Art Centre's 2019 move; the Urban Planning Exhibition Center's renovation and Wednesday closure; and the SIM advice, which is now the exact opposite of what it was.

items.name: Don't plan a Wednesday city day
items.detail: Monday closure is the usual rule for Chinese museums but not universal, and the two places you'd actually want both break it: the Urban Planning Exhibition Center closes Wednesdays and the Propaganda Poster Art Centre opens daily. Monday 12 October is a park day in both plans anyway.
